Note::remove_digits¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::remove_digits() const

Delete Digit Characters From Every Cell¶

remove_digits() returns a new Note, same shape as the input, with every ASCII digit 0–9 deleted from each cell. Use it to drop version numbers, counts, IDs, or dates from text you want to compare or group by wording alone.

Only the ten ASCII digits are removed. Letters, whitespace, punctuation, and non-ASCII characters are kept, and nothing is trimmed or collapsed — so "v2.1" becomes "v." and a cell that is all digits becomes "".

remove_digits is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note.

Example 1: A Batch¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"v2.1 build 405", "no digits", "2026"}).remove_digits())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["v. build ", "no digits", ""]

"2026" is all digits, so it reduces to the empty string.

See Also¶

  • Note::keep_digits: the complement — keep only the digits.

  • Note::remove_letters / Note::remove_punctuation: drop other classes.

  • Note::contains_any_digit: test for a digit first.
